newsitem.title: USA: Most US spot resids steady, USG low sulphur gains.
newsitem.headline: Most US spot resids steady, USG low sulphur gains.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly stayed little changed Monday in thin, post-holiday trade, with demand into Florida and high sulphur interest from Mexico leaving the Gulf better supported than New York. Traders said mild East Coast weekend weather and forecasts for more of the same through the week slowed utility burns.
"The East Coast is going to have to wait for summer to return, but the Gulf seems firm on continued heat in Florida and some Mexican interest," said one cash trader.
In New York Harbor, one percent was still pegged on either side of $17 a barrel, traders said.

NYH August one percent paper slipped another 30 cents or more to the $16.30-50 area despite steady crude. September paper also was quoted lower at $16.00-25, with Q4 paper pegged at $16.50-70, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was little changed at $18.25-50.
New York high sulphurs also were steady, with 2.2 percent still talked in the low-$15s.

At the U.S. Gulf, one percent firmed 35 cents to near the $16 level on recent heat in Florida and reports a utility there would tender Tuesday for 200,000 barrels of one percent and a small quantity of diesel. Other tender details were unknown.
USG three percent was flat from Thursday at $13.75, but traders said Mexican buying continued to support the grade.

New York city gate swing gas prices gained a couple of cents Monday to the high-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $15.00 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was up a similar amount to about $2.13/mmBtu, or $13.42 a barrel.
